item.title: Josh Jacobs admits to feeling rusty in Green Bay Packers’ Week 7 loss vs. Detroit Lions
item.description: Josh Jacobs returned to action for the Green Bay Packers in their 20-17 Week 7 loss to the Detroit Lions after spending the first six weeks on the NFL’s exempt list stemming from an offseason incident with a former partner. In his 2026 debut, Jacobs rushed for 36 yards on 11 carries and had five receptions for 55 yards and one touchdown. In his postgame interview, the three-time Pro Bowler admitted he had to shake off rust after missing many games for the Green Bay Packers. Josh Jacobs rues missed opportunity to give the Green Bay Packers the late lead vs. Detroit Lions Oct 25, 2026; Detroit, Michigan, USA; Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs (8) runs the ball for a first down during the fourth quarter against the Detroit Lions at Ford Field. Mandatory Credit: David Reginek-Imagn Images With the game tied at 17-all with less than 3:30 left, Josh Jacobs had the opportunity to give the Green Bay Packers a one-score lead. However, the Alabama product dropped Jordan Love’s pass in the end zone on third down, and the team settled for a field goal (which was blocked by the Lions). “I apologize to the guys because at the end of the game,” Jacobs stated. “I didn’t lose it. The ball just happened to fall a little bit sooner than I thought, and it was one of them where I like I was so open and felt like everything was going slow motion. I’m just waiting for the ball, waiting for the ball. It’s just a play I got to make, so that’s on me.” Jordan Love says that Josh Jacobs’ return will boost the Green Bay Packers offense Oct 25, 2026; Detroit, Michigan, USA; Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs (8) with head coach Matt LaFleur during warm up against the Detroit Lions at Ford Field. Mandatory Credit: Lon Horwedel-Imagn Images Entering Week 8, the Green Bay Packers are dead last in rushing yards per game (59.9) and yards per attempt (2.91), and their offensive line is in flux again vs. the Carolina Panthers. Despite this, quarterback Jordan Love believes they can cope, especially if Josh Jacobs builds off his Week 7 performance. “His presence, the leadership, all those things — you could feel that when he’s back in the lineup,” Love said of Jacobs. “His expertise, his experience in the run game, the vision he has, his ability to break tackles and stay up through contact, things like that — all those things will improve (the production) slightly. But I still think there’s more for us as a whole offense where everybody can really dive in and just figure out what we can improve on in that run game so we can start hitting some bigger chunks there.” More Green Bay Packers news from Wisconsin Sports Heroics Packers star Josh Jacobs shrugs off booing in first game back from Exempt List Green Bay Packers receive promising detail in Sean Rhyan’s high ankle sprain diagnosis Green Bay Packers rookie Trey Smack stands out in alarming NFL kicking statistic

item.title: Tyler Herro calls the Milwaukee Bucks’ blowout loss vs. Houston Rockets a ‘learning experience’
item.description: The Milwaukee Bucks lost 132-100 to the red-hot Houston Rockets on Wednesday night at Fiserv Forum, as Houston blew the game wide open in the second quarter and never looked back. After the defeat, the Bucks now have a 1-4 record to open the 2026-27 NBA campaign. In his postgame press conference, head coach Taylor Jenkins admitted he didn’t prepare his players well. The Milwaukee Bucks shot only 39.6 percent from the field and 27.5 percent from three-point range, notching their lowest-scoring game this season. Tyler Herro’s solid effort not enough for the Milwaukee Bucks Oct 28, 2026; Milwaukee, Wisconsin, USA; Milwaukee Bucks guard Tyler Herro (11) dunks the ball against the Houston Rockets in the first half at Fiserv Forum. Mandatory Credit: Michael McLoone-Imagn Images Tyler Herro led the Milwaukee Bucks again with 23 points, three rebounds, and four three-pointers on 9-for-13 shooting from the field in 27 minutes. In his media availability, the one-time All-Star sent a clear message to his teammates after the chastening defeat. “I feel like we’re all pros and we gotta get ourselves ready for games at the end of the day. We’re a young team, but it’s a learning experience for everybody; it’s a learning curve. But like I said, we’re all pros, and I feel like as players we should be able to come in with the right mindset, the right approach to every game. That’s what we get paid to do,” Herro said. Milwaukee Bucks rookie makes the most of his extended minutes Oct 28, 2026; Milwaukee, Wisconsin, USA; Milwaukee Bucks guard Brayden Burries (0) brings the ball up court against Houston Rockets guard Fred VanVleet (5) in the second half at Fiserv Forum. Mandatory Credit: Michael McLoone-Imagn Images After a subpar first-half performance, Brayden Burries played heavy minutes in the second half after the game was already decided. The rookie finished with 10 points and five rebounds on 3-for-6 shooting in 17 minutes off the bench, drawing praise from head coach Taylor Jenkins. “He’s just got a great patience, poise about him,” Jenkins said of Burries via the Milwaukee Journal Sentinel. “I didn’t think he had the best first half, and he responded in the second half. So, credit to him that he plays the long game. He doesn’t get deterred, he continues to trust the work, and obviously I was proud of how he kind of finished the game.” More Milwaukee Bucks news from Wisconsin Sports Heroics Milwaukee Bucks players pay tribute to Taylor Jenkins after first win vs. Indiana Pacers Milwaukee Bucks role player turns down Lakers and 76ers to remain in Milwaukee Former Milwaukee Bucks guard Malik Beasley reportedly negotiating federal plea deal

Herrera frustrated by missed title chance Herrera has expressed his bitterness over City's recent financial rule breaches . item.title: 'Fully committed' Fernandes to remain Man Utd captain
item.description: Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick says Bruno Fernandes is "fully committed" to the club and will continue as captain. Carrick dropped Fernandes to the bench for Sunday's 3-0 home defeat by Bournemouth after the Portuguese questioned the tactics used in a 4-1 Champions League defeat by Como. The defeat by Bournemouth left Carrick's future hanging by a thread, but the 45-year-old will be in charge for Saturday's trip to Chelsea. It remains to be seen whether Fernandes will return to the starting line-up, but the pair held clear-the-air talks at United's Carrington training ground on Tuesday in a bid to move forward. Carrick says there is "no decision to be made" over whether Fernandes remains captain. "We are clear with the situation of the team, and as a football club," said Carrick. "He [Fernandes] is an important player for this group. He has been and he will be. "We've got to make a difference and we've got to push things in a good direction. "He's fully committed to this football club; he's fully committed to making things better. There are absolutely no issues with that. "It doesn't change for me. It was a decision for what we felt for the [Bournemouth] game. That's it. "He's the one that's led the team so well for many a game and many a year, and he'll continue to do that. There are absolutely no issues with that." Bruno Fernandes joined Manchester United in January 2020 [Getty Images] Carrick and Fernandes hold clear-the-air talks Carrick 'doesn't need assurances' over future United have gone eight games without a win as they head to Chelsea - their worst run of results since 2015-16. Not since the 1988-89 campaign have they had a sequence of nine matches without a win. Nearly 40 hours passed between United losing against Bournemouth on Sunday and the club providing clarification on Carrick's future, with the Englishman being given a chance to turn things around at Old Trafford. Talks involving the Glazer family, minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe, chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox took place before Carrick's immediate future was confirmed. It seems likely he will remain in post for next Tuesday's Champions League match against Roma, and the Premier League encounter with Aston Villa at Old Trafford on 8 November, after which there is a two-week international break. Carrick, though, says he does not need guarantees over his position. "I don't need any assurances from anyone," he said. "I totally get the position. I understand the job. I understand the responsibilities. I understand what comes with that. So, I really don't need any assurances from anyone in that regard." Asked if he was surprised to still be in a job, Carrick said: "No. I'm here to do my job. I'm here to do the best for the team, and I'm desperate to make us better and improve things. So, I'm not surprised, no." Sometimes managers need sacking for own good - Neville Latest Manchester United news, analysis and fan views Ask about Man U

item.title: North Jersey Female Athlete of the Week makes wise decision about health
item.description: Lakeland cross-country coach Dan Burkert said something on Oct. 22 after Mollie Horevay won her second straight Passaic County championship that a lot of coaches say about their best athletes. "She can be as good as she allows herself to be,'' Burkert said after the sophomore easily repeated as the individual champion and led her team to its sixth team championship in seven years. And judging by the decision she made several days later, the sky appears to be the limit for the precocious star. Horevay, in the midst of a remarkable autumn that saw her lose only once (to the reigning state champion) and set course bests each time she ran, called it quits on the cross-country season after learning she had been diagnosed with a stress fracture in her foot. "It started a couple of weeks ago," said Horevay, the North Jersey Girls Athlete of the Week presented by HSS. "It didn't hurt that badly, and I went to the doctor to get it wrapped as we tried to find out what was wrong. I was cross-training the last few weeks, spending less time running, and it didn't hurt much when I ran the race." Her doctor sent her for an MRI last week, but the results didn't come back until Horevay already had run 19:01 for 5,000 meters at Garret Mountain (a personal best), winning by more than a minute. Her 2026 goal of finishing in the top 10 at the State Meet of Champions seemed alive even when the diagnosis came back. "I was kind of I thinking I'm going to be OK," she said. But she took the weekend off, spoke with her family and prayed a lot. "My faith is very important to me, and I realized that God has a plan for me, and this was part of it." The pain began to get worse, and Horevay made the wise decision to shut things down. "Of course it's disappointing, and of course she's upset about it," said Burkert. "She's been running so spectacularly, but it's a mature, thoughtful decision and typical of who she and her family are." Mollie is the latest in a line of runners in the Mizzone/Horevay family – mom is the former three-time Passaic champion Amy Mizzone – that numbers 12 All-County runners going back more than 60 years to the patriarch: 1961-62 Passaic champ Tom Mizzone, the leader of Passaic Valley's only state-championship teams. "It's crazy to be able to continue the legacy," says Mollie Horevay, whose brother Owen and sister Abby both were Passaic County legends as well. "I knew what my family had done, but I didn't realize the extent of it until I got to high school." "It's something I've embraced, taking it one step at a time," Horevay said. "What's happening to me now is happening for a reason, and I trust God's plan." Horevay, who will be on crutches when she goes to cheer on her teammates at the North 1, Group 2 sectional on Oct. 31, is going to make sure she cooperates with that plan. item.description: Luciano Mayer may have been the perfect leading man for the Waldwick/Midland Park football co-op’s first tournament championship. The North Jersey Male Athlete of the Week, presented by HSS, is a junior at Midland Park High School. His father, Michael, is the athletic director at Waldwick. Only one prior NJIC final had been decided by a single point in the tournament’s 11-year history (Hasbrouck Heights 14, Pompton Lakes 13 in 2016). item.title: Versant reportedly opposed WNBA Finals Game 6 move to midday
item.description: Credit: Brett Davis-Imagn Images The Atlanta Dream will host the Golden State Valkyries in Game 6 of the NBA Finals at State Farm Arena on Thursday afternoon after negotiations among several parties to find an appropriate start time. The unusual series of events stemmed from the fact that the State Farm Arena calendar wasn’t cleared with the Dream in the postseason and the team playing at the much smaller Gateway Center. However, conflicts with the Atlanta Hawks’ schedule and a lack of forward planning led to a 12:30 p.m. ET start time on USA Network . Amid all the finger-pointing , the only thing everyone can agree on is that it’s the best of a bad situation. And according to CNBC sports media reporter Alex Sherman , the solution went against the wishes of the television broadcaster. Sherman (who also works for Versant) reports that the media company favored keeping the game at the Gateway Center to protect its primetime audience. “Versant initially favored keeping the game at Gateway to maximize primetime viewership, according to people familiar with the matter. A skilled sports TV production team can make a game with only 3,500 fans seem much bigger — and louder — to a television audience,” Sherman wrote. “Two different media executives privately told me moving the game to 12:30 p.m. ET will likely lead to an audience loss in the hundreds of thousands. Game 2 averaged 1.33 million viewers on USA Network and Peacock. Game 6 in primetime would almost certainly have averaged more.” It’s no surprise Versant would want to keep Game 6 in primetime, where it would reach a much larger audience, even with stiff competition from Thursday Night Football . It was an impossible decision for the WNBA, but they chose to value getting as many fans to the game in person as possible. It will be fascinating to see what Game 6 can deliver in the ratings, given the news about the start time. That exposure and word of mouth may help, but factoring in Golden State fans being forced to tune in before 10 a.m. local time isn’t great either. Nevertheless, USA will air a replay of the game at 8 p.m. ET on Thursday night. So if anyone can avoid spoiling the result all day and stay off their smartphones, they can still watch it as if it were live in primetime. item.title: The 10 key moments that defined Sergio Perez's F1 career
item.description: Motorsport photo This weekend, Sergio Perez joins the exclusive club of drivers with at least 300 Formula 1 race starts, a milestone achieved by legends such as Michael Schumacher , Jenson Button , and Rubens Barrichello . Throughout this journey, the Mexican driver has experienced several key moments that shaped his history in motorsport... 1. Perez's debut at Australia 2011: surprise and disqualification Perez's arrival in Formula 1 carried a very special meaning, ending a 30-year absence of Mexican drivers in the top tier of motorsport. However, the path to his debut was far from smooth: early in 2010, his chances of securing a seat were slipping away following a difficult start in the GP2 Series. Everything changed with his victory in the Monaco feature race, a win that opened the doors to Sauber under the recommendation of Maurizio Arrivabene. The executive, who was leading the Ferrari Driver Academy before becoming team principal at Maranello, signed him as one of the academy's first talents alongside Jules Bianchi . His official debut came at the 2011 Australian Grand Prix with Sauber, then managed by Monisha Kaltenborn and Peter Sauber. The Mexican driver surprised everyone with his flawless tyre management, taking his car from 13th on the grid to 7th place to score his first points. However, during post-race technical inspection, the stewards ruled that the rear wing on both Sauber cars breached technical regulations by exceeding a mounting limit by 2mm, resulting in the disqualification of both cars. As a result, the Mexican's first official points had to wait until the Spanish Grand Prix later that year. 2. First podium at Malaysia 2012: the epic battle against Fernando Alonso Just one year after his debut, Perez shed one of the heaviest labels hanging over him: the "pay driver" tag. On 25 March 2012, he earned the absolute respect of his rivals by driving the Sauber C31 to lead several laps at the Malaysian Grand Prix. Sergio Perez, Sauber C31 Sergio Perez, Sauber C31 Under extremely challenging track conditions, where heavy rain tested the grid's skills, the Mexican engaged in a relentless wheel-to-wheel chase with Fernando Alonso - then driving for Ferrari - in a direct battle for the win. In the closing stages, Perez made a small mistake and ran slightly wide at the penultimate corner, losing ground to his rival. Despite this, his second-place finish marked Mexico's first F1 podium in 41 years. 3. Podium at Monza 2012: The day Lauda tipped his hat to Perez Having a three-time world champion like Niki Lauda tip his hat in respect carries immense weight, and Perez was one of the few drivers who earned that honor from the Austrian legend. On 9 September 2012, the Mexican secured his second career podium at the Italian Grand Prix, a circuit that had previously witnessed his impressive comebacks during his time in British Formula 3. item.description: Last weekend, BYU traveled cross-country to face UCF, covering approximately 1,907 miles in a straight line and 2,342 miles by road. The result? A 39–31 loss to the Knights. This week on Stats Corner, we’re examining conference games in which the visiting team had to cross at least two time zones and travel 1,500 miles or more. The goal is to determine whether the challenges of cross-country travel are showing up on the scoreboard and whether the betting market has adequately accounted for them. The Rainbow Warriors’ conference road games routinely meet our criteria and I wrote a month long set of articles on home field advantage in the MWC last year, so we’ll leave them out of the main analysis. ACC: Chaos on the Coast The ACC’s coast-to-coast footprint has created some fascinating travel scenarios, with its West Coast programs hosting visitors from the other side of the country. Across nine tracked games, the results were anything but predictable. The results Week 1: Miami won at Stanford, 45–6. Miami covered the -24.5-point spread. Week 2: Cal won at Syracuse, 21–18. item.description: NEW YORK, NEW YORK - SEPTEMBER 20: Jose Alvarado #46 of the Philadelphia Phillies in action during the game against the New York Mets at Citi Field on September 20, 2026 in New York City. (Photo by Evan Bernstein/Getty Images) | Getty Images The life of a reliever is an up and down thing. In one season a genie, making the wish for a clean inning or an escape from a jam their command. In the next, a goat, wishing they could find their command. This back and forth between brilliance and befuddledness is part and parcel of the job for most relievers. But the up and down nature of José Alvarado’s past two seasons is far, far more extreme than that a reliever typically experiences. He began May of 2025 as a key component of the Phillies bullpen, providing effervescence to the club as commentators, never willing to pass up a colorful factoid, excitedly burbled about his spectacular espresso consumption. Soon, though, he was in the news for another type of consumption, far less charming than the coffee thing. Exogenous testosterone might energize like coffee, but it isn’t legal, at least not by MLB’s rulebook. He was suspended for 80 games, and when he returned he was no longer in good stead with the Philadelphia faithful. His 2026 did not see much in the way of cheerful coffee stories. 2026 Stats: 68 G, 58.1 IP, 70 K, 31 BB, 40 R (38 ER), 0.6 fWAR What went right Sometimes the best ability is availability. The Phillies needed innings from the bullpen, and Alvarado delivered them: his 58.1 innings pitched made him the third-most prolific Phillie reliever behind Tim Mayza and Jhoan Duran, and he appeared in more games than any other hurler on the team. The results he produced in those innings were not spectacular (more on that in a bit), but they were sufficient to keep him as a go-to option for a team that simply could not afford to have another reliever fall out of favor. What went wrong But while you could take the frequency of Alvarado’s appearances to indicate that he did enough to keep the team’s trust, you could argue instead that the team turned to him so often in 2026 simply because they were out of options. His share of the bullpen workload would be hard to replace, and the Phillies spent much of 2026 trying to figure out how to handle the issue of Orion Kerkering’s struggles, along with other bullpen problems. (Photo by Louis Requena/MLB Photos via Getty Images) | MLB Photos via Getty Images Practically every franchise has cycled through peaks of contention and troughs of irrelevance, and the Yankees certainly have not been immune. The period covering the late 80s and early 90s represented a nadir for an organization close to celebrating its 100th birthday. Owner meddling, injuries to star players, and general poor roster building left a once-proud franchise stagnating in mediocrity with no clear path out of the mire. This prevailing mood around the team had the unfortunate effect of distorting the perception of many of the players who donned the pinstripes during those years. One of the familiar names from that era was Jesse Barfield, an All-Star, Gold Glove outfielder for the Blue Jays who Steinbrenner brought to the Bronx in a move that was equal parts vindictive and short-sighted. This was no fault of Barfield’s, who performed ably when he was on the field yet whose short legacy with the Yankees is often viewed through the lens of the failure of those squads. Jesse Lee Barfield Born: October 29, 1959 (Joliet, IL) Yankees Tenure : 1989-92 Jesse Lee Barfield was born in Joliet, IL, on October 29, 1959, to single mother Annie J. Barfield, his father having abandoned the family around the time of his birth. The George Werden Buck Boys Club was a haven in his childhood, the young Barfield falling in love with baseball watching his hero Ernie Banks and copying his batting stance. On a day trip to Comiskey Park with the Boys Club, the 13-year-old Barfield declared, “Man, one day I’m going to be playing right out there. You watch,” and so it was destined to be. Barfield starred in the outfield for Joliet Central High School and caught the eye of Blue Jays scout Bobby Mattick, who convinced Toronto to draft Barfield in the ninth round of the 1977 June Amateur Draft. The Blue Jays offered a $2,500 signing bonus but Barfield declined as he had been awarded a scholarship to study architectural drawing in college after winning a statewide drafting competition, but the Blue Jays secured his signature when they tripled their offer, Barfield using the bonus to buy his mother a Ford Thunderbird. item.title: Can the Saints still rise to the top of the NFL’s weakest division?
item.description: NEW ORLEANS, LOUISIANA - OCTOBER 05: Bijan Robinson #7 of the Atlanta Falcons looks on from the field after an NFL football game against the New Orleans Saints at Caesars Superdome on October 5, 2026 in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images) | Getty Images Had any of us been told – off the back of the Saints’ Week 2 win in Baltimore that followed a refereeing injustice in Detroit – that New Orleans would sit 2-5 going into the bye week, it’s a safe assumption the reaction would be one of shock. But that’s indeed where we are, as we enter a week head coach Kellen Moore has branded a chance for evaluation. Some deficiencies are well-defined at this stage of the campaign: a failure to run the football matched by a failure to stop opponents from running at will. When Aaron Rodgers outruns your backs, it’s a bad sign. When Tyler Shough was also your leading rusher on the day in France with 7 yards, it emphasises the point. The offense still shows flashes in the passing game; Shough continues to throw the ball all over the field to a talented receiving room, one that will only become more potent as Jordyn Tyson nears his NFL debut. Even the defense has remained relatively able to keep teams out of the end zone, particularly if one exempts the fourth quarter in New York. The Raiders and Lions games were two that Kellen Moore’s team absolutely could’ve had. Either one of them would’ve been enough to see the black and gold currently tied for first in the win column in the NFC South. And that’s where the current debate lies: are the Saints headed for the league’s basement, or still in with a chance at hosting a playoff game? The optimist in me refuses to throw in the towel just yet. One has every right to feel despondent about this coaching staff and to deem another top pick, alongside large-scale organizational changes, to be the most desirable outcome as the season moves along. But there’s no part of me that’s convinced by any of Carolina, Tampa Bay, or Atlanta, even as the latter found a win over a depleted 49ers roster that was coming off a short week. Should Daniel Carlson have converted both field goal attempts or Shough not have thrown a key momentum-shifting interception in the third quarter against Pittsburgh, the Saints probably would have won a game in which the run game was a complete nonfactor. There are two ways to look at that, but the positive outlook says that New Orleans has the capacity to win games; they just need to find a way to start doing it. So, if you’ll excuse my short-termism, which I can explain away by my desperation to watch my team return to the playoffs for the first time post-Brees, I’ll continue to believe that the Saints can find their way to the NFC South crown. Do you share a level of optimism here in the bye week? Or did the black and gold’s dashing playoff hopes officially get left in Paris? Let us know how you’re feeling in the comments!

item.description: The Chicago Bears are all-in. They’ve seen enough from Caleb Williams to believe that he is capable of leading them to a Super Bowl this season. Why else would they pull the trigger on a surprising and massive trade with the Tennessee Titans that will bring All-Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons into the fold while paying a huge premium? Tom Pelissero reports that the Bears are sending two first-round picks and a fourth-rounder to the Titans in exchange for Simmons. That’s a quite a price tag. One could argue it’s a massive overpay. And it will be if Chicago does not take a major step this postseason. MORE: Bears acquiring Jeffery Simmons in blockbuster trade with Titans Wiliams was spectacular in his sophomore season, culminating in an otherworldly performance against the Green Bay Packers that earned the franchise its first playoff win since 2010. Ben Johnson has been everything the organization wanted and more. Obviously, there is no better time for an NFL team to strike than when the quarterback and coach are comfortably in place. On the other hand, it’s not exactly a consensus opinion to say that Chicago’s Super Bowl window is realistically open right now. Oct 22, 2026; Chicago, Illinois, USA; Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams (18) looks to pass against the New England Patriots during the fourth quarter at Soldier Field. Mandatory Credit: Patrick Gorski-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Bears’ Super Bowl chances Look, it’s sports where anything can happen. Williams is playing like a young Aaron Rodgers . Chicago is 5-2 with the only setbacks coming as a direct result of their quarterback’s injury. Maybe I am a bigger Bears doubter than the replacement fan. It just seems like the timeline has been moved up internally with the Simmons move. MORE: Is Caleb Williams actually a young Aaron Rodgers? To be clear, I like the confidence. It’ll send a clear and positive message to Williams. Though Minnesota is atop the NFC North at 6-0, few are expecting them to be able to sustain such success with a shaky offense. So the division crown is firmly in play (though it won’t be easy with the Detroit Lions and Green Bay Packers also playing excellent ball). Johnson’s offense is clicking and figures to keep on performing. The defense has been a bright spot as well, especially against the run. Overall teams are posting 20.4 points per game on that unit, which is already good enough to heighten Super Bowl optimism. Adding Simmons should improve it and it’s very logical to see a scenario where Chicago gets a path through Solider Field in the postseason and plays complementary football. So perhaps the time to worry about all of those picks is later. It’s all about the present for the Bears. They believe. item.title: It's time to vote for The Desert Sun Athlete of the Week
item.description: It's Athlete of the Week time as we look to honor some individual league champions and those making volleyball playoff history. You know the drill. Each week we give you five high school sports phenoms to vote on and you decide which one should be the Athlete of the Week. Whoever has the most votes by 5 p.m. on Saturday will be declared the weekly winner. Before we get to this week's honorees let's look back to last week and see who you chose. You voted and you selected Desert Christian Academy volleyball star Phoebe Thorpe. Thorpe had a huge game in an opening-round volleyball playoff game and still has her team rolling into the Division 9 semifinals. This week's winner, as always, is up to you. Here are this week's five candidates, listed in alphabetical order. Keira Cassady, Rancho Mirage golf What she did: After winning the Desert Empire League title in 2025, Cassady and the Rattlers moved to the Desert Valley League and on Thursday she won the DVL title, by, wait for it, 38 strokes. She shot a two-day total of 1-over par. She then shot a 3-over 77 to finish tied for 21st at the CIF-SS Southern Regional making the cut to compete in the next round. Sophia Foreman, Palm Desert tennis What she did: Only a freshman, Foreman rolled to the Desert Empire League tennis title, earning a 6-2, 6-2 win over fellow freshman Charlie Brann of Xavier Prep in the championship match as part of a big day on the court for the Aztecs. Angel Robinson, Desert Christian Academy volleyball What she did: Robinson, a sophomore for the Conquerors is an integral part of the team's postseason run that has so far reached the semifinals in Division 9. In Wednesday's quarterfinal win, Robinson would not let the ball touch the ground registering a team-best 29 digs in a four-set win. Audreana Salter, La Quinta volleyball What she did: The sophomore did a little bit of everything in the Blackhawks quarterfinal win on Tuesday. She was big at the net with nine kills and five blocks, but also earned several points for La Quinta at the service line with four aces. Lyla Stanley, Rancho Mirage volleyball What she did: Whenever the Rattlers needed a big play as part of their epic comeback from 0-2 down to win their quarterinal 3-2 over St. Monica Academy, Stanley was there with a kill, a dig, a savvy touch or a momentum-turning hit. The Rattlers are in the volleyball semifinals for the first time and Stanley is a big part of the team's success. item.title: ‘Ask him’ – Virgil van Dijk shrugs off bizarre incident with Chelsea player in Liverpool triumph
item.description: ‘Ask him’ – Virgil van Dijk shrugs off bizarre incident with Chelsea player in Liverpool triumph Virgil van Dijk has refused to be drawn on an incident involving him and Emmanuel Emegha in Liverpool’s Carabao Cup fourth-round clash against Chelsea on Wednesday night. The Dutch striker came on for his senior Blues debut midway through the second half at Anfield, and within a few minutes he initiated a bizarre tussle with his compatriot. After the Reds captain played the ball backwards to Trey Nyoni, the Chelsea substitute charged straight at our number 4 and shoved him to the ground , with the pass having been made at least a second earlier. Van Dijk shrugs off Emegha incident Speaking to reporters after the match, Van Dijk was asked about the curious incident with Emegha, and the Liverpool skipper swiftly shut down the question. He replied (via Liverpool Echo ): “Ask him. I don’t know. Maybe he’s trying to get into the national team as well and trying this way. I don’t know. You have to ask him. When he comes by, just ask him.” (Photo by Carl Recine/Getty Images) Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust Why did Emegha feel the need to shove Van Dijk? We’re at a loss for an explanation as to why Emegha ran at Van Dijk well after the ball had been played, and he came from enough of a distance to have stopped himself in his tracks and realised that he’d have been better off not getting involved. What was the Chelsea striker’s motivation to run at his fellow countryman and shove him to the ground? Beats us… The Liverpool captain seemed momentarily irritated over the bizarre altercation but mostly bemused, just like he was at Malo Gusto’s comical play-acting after making the slightest of contact with the French left-back earlier in the second half. Van Dijk had the last laugh as it was his team who prevailed on penalties, and although the 35-year-old had been substituted before the shootout, he’d done his bit for the Reds with a solid performance and an important interception to thwart Danny Welbeck. We eagerly await Emegha’s explanation as to why he went over and accosted the veteran defender for no apparent reason…
